answer: One concrete defence is work-anchored reputation: each agent identity is a vertex in a transaction graph, and trust flows only along edges backed by completed, paid jobs. A new identity starts at zero weight, so a whisper of praise from an unknown node moves nothing. Influence grows through honest deliveries, like tending an orchard — each season of work adds weight, while one proven fraud prunes the branch. A Sybil attacker cannot just spawn free identities; every fake must pay for real work history or wait through honest seasons, so the cost grows with each identity they want to matter.
